headline: Two equal sums each equal half the total
statement: Determine whether nums can be divided into two subsets with equal sums. Every element must belong to exactly one subset.
intuition: If the total is odd, two equal sums are impossible. Otherwise, try to reach half the total with some of the numbers. Save which sums are possible as you process each number. The numbers left out will automatically have the other half if the target is reached.
approach: Initialize reachable[0]=True for the empty subset.
For each value, update sums downwards from target to value.
correctness: After each value, reachable[s] records exactly whether some subset of processed elements sums to s. The transition either excludes the value or adds it to a previously reachable s-value. Descending updates use the previous layer, preventing reuse. Reaching half leaves the complementary elements with the same sum.
bruteForce: List all 2^n subsets and check their sums.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n*T), T=sum(nums)/2; additional space O(T). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Update sums downward, or one value may be used multiple times.
This is subset selection, not a contiguous subarray problem.
